newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF, Kampo to delay Nomura action until probe ends.
newsitem.headline: MOF, Kampo to delay Nomura action until probe ends.

text.p: Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday they would wait for the outcome of a probe by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) before deciding whether to suspend their bond business with Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
"The bureau will wait for the outcome of the SESC probe and MOF's official measures against Nomura before taking any punitive action," a Kampo official told Reuters.
Such measures could include suspending the bureau's bond lending business with Nomura, he added.
A MOF official said the ministry would also wait for the conclusion of the SESC's probe before taking any possible steps against Nomura.
He added that in 1991, when Nomura was involved in a similar incident, MOF banned Nomura from underwriting Japanese government bonds for two months.

Nomura said last week that two of its directors had made deals that appeared to be "discretionary" transactions, meaning they were done without the client's knowledge, and moved profits raised from Nomura's own funds into a corporate client's account, practices banned under Japan's securities law. Media reports have linked the corporate client with a former "sokaiya" racketeer.
Major Japanese asset management firms, including Nomura's own unit Nomura Investment Management Co, said on Monday they had suspended business with Nomura Securities after the latest incident.
